alignments.note: Existential הָיָה carries the recast 'shall have' (rule 43).
The possessive לְ is left with no English by the 'have' recasting (rules 40, 43).
Suffix takes the subject pronoun of the recasting (rules 18, 43).
The negation is recast onto the object nominal as the determiner 'no' (rule 15).
Preposition plus construct noun fused to one English word (rule 30), headed on the construct noun (rule 23).
Proper name, the written subject of the verbless clause; it takes the English noun realizing it and nothing more (rule 20).

The clause writes its subject twice, as יְהוָה and as this resuming pronoun, and the ASV realizes it once, as 'Jehovah'; the pronoun is therefore the unrendered occurrence (rule 22). The competing reading gives the single 'is' to this pronoun as the morpheme standing where an English copula stands, but rule 20 sends a construction-supplied copula to the predicate, and a copula answers to the predication rather than to the pronoun.
Predicate noun takes the construction-supplied copula, discontinuous around the possessive (rules 20, 25), exactly as הַדָּבָר takes 'is ... thing' around its article at DEU.18.22.
כַּאֲשֶׁר fused to 'as', headed on the governing opening morpheme (rule 23).
Finite verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17).

review_notes: The copula of יְהוָה הוּא נַחֲלָתוֹ is placed on the predicate נַחֲלָת and the resuming הוּא marked unrepresented, matching DEU.18.3, DEU.18.12 and DEU.18.22 and following rules 20 and 22; the competing reading, which gave 'is' to the pronoun, is named in that unit's note.
The clause is recast possessively: הָיָה takes 'shall have' and its לְ goes unrepresented (rules 40, 43).
